critical_code_review_comments: hk_dispatch.run_dispatch_internal: departure query includes status 'checked_in' — this dispatches HK cleaning tasks for guests who never actually checked out but merely had check_out==today; if a guest overstays (day-use extension after 15:00) or receptionist forgot to hit checkout, HK will be dispatched prematurely. Consider limiting to status='checked_out' or gating on time-of-day.

hk_dispatch.board: 'minutes' calculation `sum(... for t in mine if t not in done)` compares dicts by identity — this works because 'done' list contains the same object refs as 'mine', but is fragile. Use a set of task ids for clarity.

res_quality.scan_internal: duplicate detection groups by guest_email OR guest_name — if two different guests happen to share a first-name-only guest_name and same check_in/property, false positive 'duplicate' will be reported. Recommend requiring email match only.

res_quality.autofix_internal: silently ignores properties that have no matching guest_profile (correct behavior) but never records to res_quality_log which issues were left unfixed — the log entry only holds counters. Add {unfixed_email_ids, unfixed_phone_ids} for auditability.

automation_roi time-saved endpoint (~line 345): action counts appear to be derived from actual DB rows — verify hk_dispatch counter increments per dispatched task rather than per run, otherwise long-term FTE will under-report as usage grows.

hk_dispatch does not persist a per-run summary anywhere — historical dispatch analytics (how many tasks/day, urgent%, distribution fairness) are lost. Consider inserting a run summary into a hk_dispatch_log collection for reporting.
